data.summary: In late October, Novaya Gazeta announced it was closing. On November 5, World Digital Preservation Day, RIMA and Kronika are making the complete Novaya Gazeta archive available, including previously unavailable issues. They are now all collected in one place, free to read and fully searchable. One of the most unforgettable stories the outlet ever ran, back when it was called Novaya Ezhednevnaya Gazeta (New Daily Gazette), was its investigation of Russia’s black market in nuclear arms. Co-author Kirill Belyaninov told Meduza how he, Dmitry Muratov, and columnist Vladimir Filin set out to buy the makings of a nuclear bomb from Moscow middlemen.

This year’s budget deficit will turn out to be roughly twice as large as authorities had expected, and will remain significant in the coming years. Because of the sanctions, the state is missing out on trillions of rubles. Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries and other targets deep inside the country are also inflicting substantial damage. Nevertheless, the ruble has been strengthening against the dollar and the euro in recent months and has regularly ranked among the world’s strongest currencies in 2026. Eskov and Nagornov face five to ten years in prison. Photographs of special trains — including Vladimir Putin’s armored train, the subject of a 2023 investigation by the Russian investigative outlet Dossier Center — have repeatedly appeared on RailGallery and other similar sites.

https://meduza.io/en/feature/2026/11/06/.label: Meduza: Russia’s trainspotters have spent years documenting the country’s railways. Amid the war, their hobby has put them in the crosshairs of the security services.

data.title: Meduza: Investigation finds Russia’s billboards featuring troops fighting in Ukraine include men with criminal convictions and soldiers accused of war crimes
data.summary: Billboards featuring portraits of soldiers fighting in Russia’s war in Ukraine are a common sight in Russian cities. Their stories appear on the Russian Defense Ministry’s website — but the official biographies leave out some facts. The news outlet Bumaga identified 24 soldiers featured on billboards in St. Petersburg. They include soldiers killed at the front, former prisoners awarded the title of Hero of Russia, and suspected perpetrators of war crimes in Ukraine. Meduza is translating Bumaga’s full report on these men and other soldiers featured on the Defense Ministry’s website — more than 700 in all.
